a:r.a:t: You need to know structures, names, and symbols (both two-letter (dA) and four-letter (dAMP) codes).

p:cNvPr.descr: Deoxyribonucleases (labeled below). The structures of 4 nucleosides are shown. Each nucleoside described has a phosphate group (PO4-) bonded to its left. Beginning with the structure on the left, there is text below reading, "Nucleotide: Deoxyadenylate (deoxyadenosine 5 -monophosphate). Symbols: A, dA, dAMP. Nucleoside: Deoxyadenosine (pink)." To the right of the PO4-, the rightmost O is bonded right to the pentose ring, shaded orange. O bonds right to CH2, which bonds down to C, which bonds down to H. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds right to C, which bonds up & down to H, then bonds up & right to C. C bonds down to H and has a long bond upward that connects to a second ring structure. C bonds up and left to O, which bonds down and left to the initial C. All pentose rings in the diagram share this structure. The long bond on the right bonds up to an N on a 2-imidazoline ring (cyclopentane with one double bond and 2 N). The N bonds up to C, which double bonds left to N, which bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to C, which bonds right to N. This ring bonds left to a pyrimidine ring (benzene ring with 2 N). The bottom N double bonds left to C, which bonds up to N. N double bonds right to C, which bonds right to C, which double bonds down to C, which then bonds down and left to N. The top N bonds up to NH2. These rings plus the pentose ring below are shaded orange, as this is the nucleoside. To the right is deoxyguanylate, with text below reading: "Nucleotide: Deoxyguanylate (deoxyguanosine 5'-monophosphate). Symbols: G, dG, dGMP. Nucleoside: deoxyguanosine (pink)." To the right of the PO4-, the rightmost O is bonded right to the pentose ring, shaded orange. O bonds right to CH2, which bonds down to C, which bonds down to H. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds right to C, which bonds up & down to H, then bonds up & right to C. C bonds down to H and has a long bond upward that connects to a second ring structure. C bonds up and left to O, which bonds down and left to the initial C. All pentose rings in the diagram share this structure. The long bond on the right bonds up to an N on a 2-imidazoline ring (cyclopentane with one double bond and 2 N). The N bonds up to C, which bonds down to C and bonds up to N, which bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to C, which bonds right to N. This ring bonds left to a pyrimidine ring (6-sided ring with 2 double bonds and 2 N). The bottom N double bonds left to C, which bonds down and left to NH2. C bonds up to NH. N double bonds right to C, which bonds right to C, which double bonds down to C, which then bonds down and left to N. The top C double bonds up to O. These rings plus the pentose ring below are shaded orange, as this is the nucleoside. To the right of this is the next image, with text below reading, “Deoxythymidylate (deoxythymidine 5’ monophosphate. Symbols: T, dT, dTMP. Nucleoside: deoxythymine.” To the right of the PO4-, the rightmost O is bonded right to the pentose ring, shaded orange. O bonds right to CH2, which bonds down to C, which bonds down to H. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds right to C, which bonds up & down to H, then bonds up & right to C. C bonds down to H and has a long bond upward that connects to a second ring structure. C bonds up and left to O, which bonds down and left to the initial C. All pentose rings in the diagram share this structure. The C on the right bonds up to N, which is part of a 6-sided ring with 2 Ns and 1 double bond. N bonds up & left to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up left to CH3 and up and right to C. C double bonds up to O and down & right to NH. NH bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O and down and left to the initial N. To the far right is the next image, with text below reading, "Deoxycytidilate (deoxycytidine 5'-monophosphate). Symbols: C, dC, dCMP. Nucleoside: deoxcytidine." To the right of the PO4-, the rightmost O is bonded right to the pentose ring, shaded orange. O bonds right to CH2, which bonds down to C, which bonds down to H. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds right to C, which bonds up & down to H, then bonds up & right to C. C bonds down to H and has a long bond upward that connects to a second ring structure. C bonds up and left to O, which bonds down and left to the initial C. The C that bonds up to a second ring structure bonds up to N, which is part of a 6-sided ring structure with 2 Ns and 2 double bonds. The bottom N of the ring bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds right to C, which bonds up to NH2 and double bonds down and right N, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O and down and left to C.
